claim: Sprinting is one of the very best ways to boost your hormonal profile as a man
Think primal: for optimizing hormones especially, it really helps, since much of our body and mind responds the way it would have in a primal time, not necessarily in today's world

As cavemen, sprinting meant chasing down a hunt or running from a predator, and our bodies got the message "I need to be a man right now": strength, power and the hormones to kill this bison or run away from this bear

Since primal bodies got that message from sprinting, it just makes sense that sprinting at absolute maximum effort signals our hormones to boost, and they really do: modern science shows it in the numbers we can test
Sprinting is one of the most beneficial things you can add to your life, even with no other changes to your fitness, nutrition or anything else: just add it two or three times a week
With sprinting, it's amazing how little time it takes, so there's absolutely no excuse of not having time: you either put in the effort or you don't
Studies show as little as one six-second sprint of maximum effort raised human growth hormone levels for as much as 60 minutes after, and boosts testosterone as well
Sprinting is not a lot of time, just the effort, and you'll really feel the benefits in your hormones, "I promise you"
How to sprint
Start with individual sprints of at least six seconds
The recommendation if you're not sprinting now: five sprints of six seconds, 30 seconds in total, with, say, a 5 or 10 second break between
Five six-second sprints take two minutes or less, and you can make incredible changes in your testosterone and human growth hormone levels
Sprint two or three times a week, "That's all it takes": less than 10 minutes a week for all the sprint workouts you need

Work up gradually in sprint length, eventually to maybe five 30-second sprints: still only two and a half minutes of running and maybe as much break, five minutes or less a couple of times a week, a pretty good routine with amazing results
The sprint studies measured one six-second and one 30-second sprint
In the sprint studies, the six-second sprint raised both human growth hormone and testosterone, for at least 60 minutes after
In the sprint studies, the 30-second sprint raised human growth hormone by 450% more than the six-second one, and kept it elevated 90 to 120 minutes instead of 60
Definitely work up to sprints as long as 30 seconds
Beyond 30 seconds you're more than likely not really in a full all-out sprint, it seems, "Or if you are, then man, good on you"
Ideally, for sprints, you're outside, running
The personal favorite way to sprint, and seemingly the ideal way: barefoot when possible, in a park, on the grass, which seems to put us in a solid biomechanical place with our running
In a shit ton of snow, or stuck in a hotel in the middle of the airport, an elliptical is a good backup for sprints: you can recreate sprinting pretty well on one
A little caution with a treadmill for sprints: you could try it, but absolute full speed, all-out on one seems a little sketchy
Ideally get outside to sprint, even for two minutes, even one
Go hardcore with sprints, absolutely all out, not a 60%, kind-of-running-fast

Before sprinting, depending on your fitness and flexibility, a few minutes to kind of warm up are suggested: some burpees, push-ups, jumping jacks, squats, or rolling out your legs with a massage roller
Be smart and don't pull a hamstring: walking out of the office on your lunch break after sitting all day and instantly bolting into a full hundred percent sprint is not recommended
Before sprinting, give at least a couple of minutes, depending on your condition, to loosen up the muscles
Get a sprint session in today and "I'll bet" you'll feel the difference tomorrow: probably better morning wood, that kind of energetic difference
The benefits of sprinting will certainly compound over time on a regular basis
Do some sprints today, right now: if you're listening, you have an extra 60 seconds or two minutes. Shut off the podcast two minutes early if you have to
Other benefits of sprinting: it raises your metabolism, helps burn fat, and brings cardiovascular benefits
The big reason all men should really be sprinting, it seems, is that it boosts hormones in really powerful ways, independent of any other changes

If you're already kind of kicking ass with fitness, nutrition and lifestyle, with hormones in great shape, with sprinting you'll get an even further boost, feel even stronger and have even more human growth hormone and testosterone
Conversely, if you're not in a great place hormonally, for any number of reasons, just starting with sprinting will really give you a boost in getting your hormones back into a good place
Psychologically too: if it's been a while since you really sprinted, doing five, even six-second ones, brings an amazing mental and mood boost along with the hormonal boost
There's no damn excuse not to sprint: literally a couple of minutes of effort, but you have to go hardcore
